description: Handles version 2.4 (builds on 2.3 / voice-1557d48f slide-in tongue + pocket near base hook; uses the new 1.20 gripper with top and bottom hooks). Bring the handles down further, and make the handle piece extend higher up, so it spans between the gripper's bottom and top hooks and slides in to be captured by both. Related params pebble: voice-3211a12d.

results.identified_issue: The pebble says 'Handles version 2.4' but 2.4 is already v204_generalist_parametric (voice-3211a12d), so this is v205 = 2.5, copied from v204. I ported trace_photo.py top_hook()/rail()/hook_floor_u() and RDP_SPLIT from v020, with top_hook_mirror_u as an outline param, and set outer_* and tip_thick to 1.19/1.20 values. trace_px.scad == v020's, and the right finger STL cmp-equals v020's. I read 'bring the handles down further' as: along the edge toward the base, so the foot fully seats in the base notch (u -11.4 vs 2.4's -10.6). It could also mean lower in Y across the finger; if so, add a y-offset param. I dropped the tongue/pocket, not re-oriented it, because with facing hooks any slide along u is blocked. A dovetail key running across Y is a possible follow-up, but a pocket near the edge breaches honeycomb holes. The plate trim sweeps xz(slide_h+2) so the full 37 mm plate clears the J-bottoms while it slides in. The stop strip is unioned after the trim, at y < -plate/2-fit. Part names stay *_slide, so live_render/serve_designs are unchanged. I didn't open the gallery Tune panel in a browser; only live_render.py was run (default render == exported STLs).
results.summary: Made version 2.5: the black handle now runs from the gripper's bottom hook all the way up to its top hook (41.8 mm long, was 28), with a foot in each hook, and slides on sideways so both hooks hold it.
results.detailed_description:
2.4 was already the parametric version, so this is 2.5. It's 2.4's params.json on 1.20's fingers (the wide beak, the flat-bottom taper and the top hook). The finger STL is byte-for-byte 1.20's.

The handle: the plate still has two strap slots and is still 37 mm across, but it now covers the whole straight outer edge, from the bottom notch's floor to the top notch's floor plus 1 mm at each end. Its bottom now reaches the floor of the base notch (2.4 stopped 0.8 mm short), and it reaches 13.8 mm higher. Each end is trimmed into a foot that fills its hook's notch.

One design change you should check: the two hooks face each other, so the handle can't slide down along the edge any more. That means 2.3's tongue and keyhole pocket are gone, and the hooks now do that job: both hold the handle along the edge and against being pulled outward. The handle slides on sideways, across the finger's thickness, from the flat bottom side. I also added a small stop strip on the handle's inner face. It hits the flat bottom face once the handle is home, so it can't slide out the far side. Only friction stops it sliding back out the way it came in.

New sliders: 'Top hook position' (moves the top hook, and the handle length follows it), 'Plate run past each notch floor', and 'Stop strip depth' and 'width' (depth 0 = no strip). The handle's length and foot-position sliders are gone, because the hooks now set them. All 14 geometry checks pass, including slides on without touching, held by both prongs, held by both notch floors, and the stop hits. Through-holes: 33 in the finger and 2 in the handle. Nothing has been printed.

summary: Handles version 2.4 lowers the handles further and extends the handle piece upward to span the new 1.20 gripper's bottom and top hooks. The handle should slide in and be captured by both hooks, building on the 2.3 slide-in tongue and pocket.
